sectors.note:
**TL;DR:** Energy and Technology continue to anchor market leadership, while Financials emerge as the sole sector with perfect "all-green" breadth despite a lower YTD rank.

The US sector landscape shows strong top-heavy leadership, with Energy (momentum 0.850, rank 1) and Technology (momentum 0.783, rank 2) maintaining their dominant positions. Financials (momentum 0.67, rank 7) are rotating into a position of notable strength, standing out as the only sector in the market with positive performance across all timeframes (week, month, quarter, half, and YTD). Healthcare is also showing minor positive rotation, gaining one spot to rank 8 with a momentum score of 0.47.

On the downside, Utilities (momentum 0.133) is fading rapidly, dropping one spot to rank 9 and solidifying its position as the primary momentum laggard. Defensives and cyclicals remain largely stagnant, with Consumer Defensive (momentum 0.42, rank 5) and Consumer Cyclical (momentum 0.43, rank 11) showing flat rank movement over the last five sessions.

## Strength
* **Financials Breadth:** Financials (momentum 0.67, rank 7) represent the sole "all-green" group, showing positive performance across the week, month, quarter, half, and YTD.
* **Energy Dominance:** Energy remains the absolute momentum leader with a score of 0.850 and retains its #1 YTD rank.
* **Technology Support:** Technology maintains its strong secular footprint as the second-strongest momentum performer at 0.783 (rank 2).

## Movers & Momentum
* **Healthcare Improving:** Healthcare was the only sector to improve its rank over the last five sessions, rising 1 spot to rank 8 with a momentum score of 0.47.
* **Utilities Slipping:** Utilities was the week's sole decliner, dropping 1 spot to rank 9 with a weak momentum score of 0.133.
* **Flat Mid-Pack:** Industrials (rank 3, momentum 0.40), Consumer Defensive (rank 5, momentum 0.42), and Basic Materials (rank 6, momentum 0.37) all showed zero rank change over the last five sessions.

## Divergences
* **Industrials Fatigue:** Industrials exhibit a negative divergence, holding a high YTD rank of 3 despite registering a lagging momentum score of just 0.400.
* **Financials Under-Ranking:** Financials show a positive divergence, carrying a lower YTD rank of 7 but boasting a strong 0.667 momentum score and perfect "all-green" breadth.
* **Consumer Cyclical Relative Value:** Consumer Cyclical sits at the bottom of the YTD rankings (rank 11) yet carries a momentum score of 0.433, which outpaces both Industrials (rank 3) and Consumer Defensive (rank 5).

industries.note:
**TL;DR:** Market breadth remains highly concentrated with only 25 of 144 groups in "all-green" territory, led by dominant secular trends in technology distribution and energy refining, while internet-related retail and content groups experience massive short-term momentum surges.

US equity market leadership is anchored by a select few resilient industries. Electronics & Computer Distribution (0.943 momentum) and Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing (0.938 momentum) continue to pace the market as the top sustained leaders. However, a sharp rotation is underway, characterized by aggressive weekly rank improvements in Internet Retail (+56 spots) and Internet Content & Information (+36 spots), alongside a notable rise in Software - Infrastructure (+32 spots). 

Conversely, defensive and commodity-linked sectors are losing their footing. Consumer Electronics dropped 26 spots, and Silver fell 22 spots to rank 96. Real estate and travel-adjacent areas are also under pressure, with Lodging losing 21 spots and REIT - Diversified declining 15 spots. Despite these pullbacks, early signs of stabilization are emerging in low-momentum areas like Education & Training Services and Grocery Stores, which are beginning to climb in rank.

## Strength
* **Constrained Breadth:** Only 25 of 144 industry groups are currently "all-green" (positive across the week, month, quarter, half-year, and YTD).
* **Sustained Leaders:** Electronics & Computer Distribution (0.94 momentum) and Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing (0.94 momentum) hold the top two YTD ranks, showing persistent strength alongside Steel (0.90 momentum).
* **Consumer and Service Strength:** Staffing & Employment Services (0.85 momentum) and Department Stores (0.83 momentum) remain firmly in the all-green category, indicating resilient pockets of consumer and corporate demand.

## Movers & Momentum
* **Rapid Rotations:** Internet Retail surged +56 spots to rank 52 (0.74 momentum), while Shell Companies (+44 spots to rank 35) and Internet Content & Information (+36 spots to rank 63) also booked major weekly gains.
* **Sharp Declines:** Consumer Electronics dropped -26 spots to rank 58, and Silver slid -22 spots to rank 96 with a weak 0.26 momentum score.
* **Deep Laggards:** Mortgage Finance (0.09 momentum, rank 142) and Gambling (0.11 momentum, rank 144) remain pinned to the bottom of the YTD momentum rankings.

## Divergences
* **Fading Momentum:** High-momentum groups showing early signs of distribution include REIT - Healthcare Facilities (0.62 momentum, -6 spots), Healthcare Plans (0.68 momentum, -5 spots), and Metal Fabrication (0.68 momentum, -5 spots).
* **Emerging from the Bottom:** Low-momentum groups starting to turn upward in rank include Education & Training Services (+5 spots, 0.49 momentum), Solar (+5 spots, 0.39 momentum), and Grocery Stores (+5 spots, 0.29 momentum).
* **Upstream Energy Softness:** In contrast to strong downstream refining, upstream energy services are cooling, with Oil & Gas Drilling (-3 spots, 0.61 momentum) and Oil & Gas Equipment & Services (-3 spots, 0.60 momentum) both losing rank.
